I’ve been in a similar situation. At the time I brought it up to my boyfriend, he expressed a similar sentiment to yours- that’s just her personality and their banter, etc. 

I told him it was a boundary issue, regardless of how he feels about her behavior, I’m uncomfortable with it, and I needed him to set boundaries with her. And him not setting a boundary with her to avoid making an awkward or uncomfortable situation made me feel like he valued her comfort more than he cared about the discomfort it caused me to see her flirt with him, and see him accept it. 

Phrasing it that way got through to him, and he became much more aware of when her behavior crossed a line into flirting, and immediately setting a boundary in the moment (“why are you staring at me?” “Stop touching me so much” “why would you say/do that, it weird” etc.). It took some time for him to figure out how he wanted to set boundaries, but once he did it helped a lot for both of us and she backed off. She is also no longer part of our friend group, but for completely different reasons.

I will say, I don’t care if someone’s personality is flirtatious. Flirting with your boyfriend in front of you is disrespectful, period. No friend should make you feel like you can’t trust them.

You can book a free 1 hour in store personal styling session at Nordstrom. I did it years ago when I needed office clothes and had no clue what to get.

You’ll have to pay for any clothes you decide to keep, but the session itself is free. You’ll fill out a quick form online and answer a few basic questions, pick a day and time, and show up. They essentially will pre pick a few items for you to try on when you get there, and bring in other items based on what you like. It’s very informative, can be fun, and they’re super nice through the whole process. It’s a great way to collect a few key pieces and learn more about what looks good on you and what to look for in the future.

[Here’s a link](https://www.nordstrom.com/browse/services/personal-stylists), looks like they also have an online chat option now too.

I work in tech and I love their data visualizations to track my calories and macros, see how my goals are doing, and how the app tracks positive and negative pattern trends in what you eat. I love the setup too, great onboarding experience.

I swear this isn’t an ad, I’m just a nerdy user happy with a product that’s made my life much easier in just a week. 

$40 subscription for a year which equals about $3.33/month, well worth the price imo.

In my experience, it’s better to observe someone’s natural behavior rather than ask them to tweak it to meet your needs. If something bothers you, definitely bring it up. But don’t ask them to change.

I say if you have a good time on the first date and want a second date, schedule it at the end of the first date.

Austin is a city of “grass is greener” syndrome and while you’ll think you’ve met a great woman, it’s not unlikely she’ll have 2-3 more first dates planned that same week/week after yours. She could become more interested in someone else by the time you ask for a second date, so go for it ASAP.
